# 0026. Role calls are owed on counts read from task records, and a dated call clears them whatever it says

Date: 2026-10-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

`role_triggers.py` owed a chief-engineer call on a `- Cycle N` line under `### Feedback Cycles` and cleared a call only when its question named `Cycle 3` or `Amendment N`. Over 38 window tasks in four repositories it read 0 events in the two that record cycles in stage-report headings, and it refused 3 of the 4 calls FO had made (two worded "third repair cycle", one filed under another heading). The Captain's direction on 2026-10-20 was counts from structured records, not keywords. The measurement, the per-task table and the falsified alternatives are in the task's `## Design`. This supersedes the wording-match clause of the special-role-triggers design (PR #664), which has no ADR of its own to amend.

## Decision

**Words:** 「設計時不應該過度依賴關鍵字，而是可能要依靠犯錯字數觸發，合理嗎？」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat; 「先加第一個，第二個列入評估」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat, on the engineering-reviewer model rule and the security-reviewer evaluation; at the ideation gate, 2026-10-20, D1 「同意」, D2 「第四輪」, D3 「Ａ」, D4 「Ａ」, D5 「同意」, each as the gate question recommended.

**Options considered:**
- Chief-engineer is owed at four repair passes, read as `## Stage Report: implementation` headings minus one (chosen, D2); three passes fires one more false case (go-live-consent); a sent-back count added one case and needs a free-text verdict match that leaves 105 of 410 validation reports unreadable; same-path review rounds, holds or overrides, ADR-draft headings and cross-references added no unique true catch or false-fired
- Engineering-reviewer keeps its replacing-amendment event, one line per task, cleared by a call dated no earlier than the amendment on a model no lower than the one required, or by a dated waiver (chosen)
- Model: Fable when the frontmatter says `profile: prod` or the `Surfaces:` line lists `db`, else Opus, never lower (chosen, D4); path or secret signals were not chosen (the authority-path signal marks 31 of 38 tasks, secrets have no field)
- Review rounds, two review ids with inline findings on an open task PR, also owe chief-engineer, as a last separate slice (chosen, D1)
- The four engineering-reviewer cases no count sees stay with judgment and no `Reverses:` line is added (chosen, D3)
- ADR 0021 D1 stays: stage 1 of the evaluation reads saved reports and runs no model, stage 2 waits for its result (chosen, D5)

**Recommended:** each of D1 to D5 as the gate question stated, which the Captain accepted.

A call or a waiver counts only as a `Reviewer:` line under `## FO alignment`, and a call counts by its date and model, not by its question. Later work that changes what owes a role call reads counts from committed task records and does not match phrases.

## Consequences

FO is told once per task and role, in the line `pr_watch.py tasks` already prints, until the call is recorded. A call on another question dated after an amendment now clears it. A count cannot see an authority change, a ruling reversed in another task or a new authority surface; those stay with the Captain and FO. The thresholds are in-sample on one 38-task window judged by four observers. Reopen when a batch shows an owed case the count missed twice in the same shape, or a false fire on a task whose extra passes were phases.

Amended 2026-10-22 (Captain: 「可以」 at the ideation gate of the task `merge-ask-holds-missing-clauses`, narrowing it to this one hold; 「按建議**不算**」 on D2): `delivery_gate.py check` runs `role_triggers.py` on the task folder and stem, without `--review-rounds`, and holds the merge ask while the committed task owes a chief-engineer call (four repair passes) or an engineering-reviewer call (a replacing amendment): exit 1 adds one problem line and the script's `next:` lines, exit 2 holds with its message (「可以」). Review rounds do not hold the ask; idle still prints that call (「按建議不算」). The script reads the task as committed, so an amendment not yet state-committed is not seen and a call not yet state-committed does not clear. "Told once per task and role" above still describes the idle line; a skipped call now also refuses the merge ask until the call or a dated waiver is committed.

Amended 2026-10-25 (Captain: 「都開」 on 2026-10-23 and 「可以」 on 2026-10-25 for the task `role-triggers-owe-ce-on-review-drift`; 「全准」 at its ideation gate on 2026-10-25, accepting D1 and D2 as the gate question recommended): a review-round event is cleared only by a chief-engineer call or waiver dated no earlier than the UTC date of the newest review round, which `pr_watch.py tasks` reads from the one comment list it already fetches and passes as `--drift-date`; a call about something else made before that round no longer clears it, and no file-path test is used (D1). A call made earlier on the same date as that round still clears it. Without `--drift-date` any call or waiver clears, as before; the repair-pass event keeps its undated clear. The merge ask still does not count review rounds (D2).

Amended 2026-11-02: Astra meets the Fable floor, and chief-engineer calls need opus rank or above, for both repair-pass and review-round events. The date and waiver rules stay as recorded above; see ADR 0049 for the Captain's words and the accepted model table.

Amended 2026-11-02 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：多開「完成通知」和「挑剔使用者可用 Gemini」兩張票，先前五件事照建議，可以嗎？」 at the ideation revision of `second-round-prompts-a-step-back`; then 「照建議」, answering 「決定：五張設計進實作、Gemini 這張停在這裡，四個決定都照建議嗎？要改哪件直接說。」 at its ideation approval): two validation reports with a Material or Needs decision F bullet, or two amendments whose `Supersedes:` does not start with `none`, print the three questions at idle and merge without a hold. The counts stay separate. D1 follows this record's structured-count rule and ADR 0045's F-bullet form, accepting that 5 of 13 word-detected tasks stay silent; replacing amendments count, not every relaxation. At either count's third occurrence, D2 follows the repair/amendment merge hold and existing waiver, rather than review rounds' non-hold; D3 assigns chief-engineer because an engineering-reviewer call already clears amendments whatever its question. Its one owed line carries: is what I am solving still the outcome first asked for; can this gap be tested now, or am I waiting; what breaks if this criterion or process is deleted? The opus-rank floor applies, Astra included. A call or waiver dated no earlier than the third amendment clears that event, reusing the drift-date rule; any qualifying call or waiver clears failed validations, reusing the undated repair rule. A fourth occurrence owes no second call; engineering-reviewer's amendment event stays separate. At count two, questions repeat on each run without an answer record; at three or more, a cleared event prints no reminder.

Amended 2026-11-02 (Captain: 「照建議」, answering 「決定：四件事都照建議嗎？要改哪件直接說。」 after FO proposed 「修這兩個 bug，在原本的票裡修」, recorded in `second-round-prompts-a-step-back` Captain amendment 1): each count reaches its own reminder threshold independently. A cleared event at three or more does not suppress the other event's second-occurrence reminder. Suppress a duplicate reminder only when an emitted owed-call line already carries the three questions; all model, date, waiver and merge-hold rules above remain.

Amended 2026-11-03 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：七張設計照建議進實作，但驗收到期提醒的 D7 改成『在 kc-journey-map 登記 journey-progress/v1，預算放寬為兩個 PR，kc-journey-map 那個先合併』，可以嗎？」 at the ideation gate of `diagnosis-rounds-count-toward-step-back`, accepting its D1 and D2 as recommended): dispatch records count diagnosis rounds by stage and normalized `Symptom:` header, trimming and collapsing spaces and casefolding; values starting with `none`, fenced lines and body lines do not count. At round two, `dispatch_records.py` prints the three step-back questions on stderr before each dispatch, following ADR 0027's placement at the write; folder mode checks each stage's highest-numbered record, and `--names` counts only through the named record. A record numbered two or higher without the header gets a stderr hint; only `--names --strict` holds it (D1). Idle and merge read committed records: round two advises without a hold, round three owes chief-engineer and holds the merge ask (D2). An opus-rank-or-above call or waiver under `## FO alignment`, dated no earlier than the third record's first `Dispatched:` date, clears that symptom's later rounds too; without that date any qualifying call or waiver clears. Other event families remain independent; an owed line carrying the questions suppresses duplicate reminders. With the replay's symptom name, measured added words are 48 per dispatch reminder, 21 per missing-header hint, 47 at idle/merge round two and 74 at round three; a clean dispatch, startup, after archive and the workflow template add zero. The workflow word budget is unchanged. Renamed symptoms and multiple browser runs inside one dispatch remain outside the count.

Clarified 2026-11-03 (Captain: 「照你建議」, answering 「決定：B 照原設計修，讓追加指示紀錄也算進同症狀的輪數嗎？」, Captain amendment 1 of `diagnosis-rounds-count-toward-step-back`, superseding no criterion): a supported `<stage>-N-message-M.md` follow-up is a dispatch round on its own symptom, as the approved design states. Both disk and committed-state readers count it; record number, then message number, gives numeric order, with the plain record before its messages. The third counted record dates clearing whether it is plain or a follow-up.
# 0070. Stage worker dispatches are built by a package script that writes their record

Date: 2026-11-07

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Three sessions left dispatch records late, reconstructed or incomplete: the
kc-paseo-plugins batch r1b-polish-1 reconstructed its records after dispatch;
the qnow observer found an unrecorded addendum; the kc-plugin observers found
late and incomplete records in batches 14 and 15. The task
`dispatch-build-writes-the-dispatch-record` records those sources.

Spacedock 0.27.2 writes the dispatch artifact but not the task's dispatch record.
It has no dispatch hook and does not read the model roster. Its stamp commit
already includes the task folder, providing a seam for a package-owned writer.
ADR 0014 keeps the package and workflow preflight checks separate, and ADR 0027
places structured write checks at the write.

## Decision

**Words:** 「核准（建議）」 — Captain, host question dialog, 2026-11-07,
batch 17 ideation approval. The question's dispatch-record excerpt was
「派工紀錄 D1 用套件裡的派工腳本並新增一份決策紀錄（ADR）、D2 模型與名冊仍由我手填、D3 版本與工作流程檢查這次不併進腳本」;
it specified 「核准即接受每張設計對其決定寫下的建議。要改哪件直接說。」.
Source: the task's ideation gate resolution, attempt 1, recorded at
2026-11-07T15:37:23.875685Z on `spacedock-state/dev2`.

**Options considered:**
- Build through a package script that writes and checks the dispatch record,
  leaving Spacedock unchanged (chosen).
- Change upstream Spacedock: outside this package; no dispatch hook exists at
  the pinned version.
- Resolve model and roster inside the script: not chosen; retain FO-supplied flags.
- Include package-version and workflow-checkout checks: not chosen; retain their
  existing separate commands and Captain-facing holds.

**Recommended:** the package script, FO-supplied model and roster, and separate
package-version and workflow-checkout checks, as accepted by the Captain.

**Protects:**
- `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/dispatch_stage.py` — `main`, the write/check/build order

FO builds stage-worker dispatches with `dispatch_stage.py`. It writes the record
from the build's checklist and scope-notes inputs, adds the supplied model and
workflow-checkout SHA, checks it, then builds. The stamp commit carries the record;
reuse-advance dispatches use `spacedock state commit` before returning the envelope.
Model and roster remain FO-supplied. The two pre-dispatch checks remain separate.

## Consequences

Record writing no longer depends on a separate manual step when FO uses the
script. This remains prose-enforced: Spacedock's skill still names its own
builder, and a direct call bypasses the writer. `dispatch_records.py --coverage`
still holds missing records after a worker report. Follow-up messages remain
manually recorded. A real-binary split-root test checks the stamp's commit seam.
Reopen on ADR 0014's condition: a dispatch-time hook in Spacedock.
# 0039. A resolved thread does not clear a Codex finding on the same head

Date: 2026-10-27

## Status

Accepted

## Context

The Codex reader previously let a later no-issues result clear a finding on the
same pull request head. The correction landed in iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins pull
request #728, merge d8e9204bfae64ab4a76ec1a2ef0357a2b8fc7b44. Its ideation
also settled whether a person's resolved mark on a GitHub review thread clears
that finding. The archive observer found this enduring ruling had no ADR.
This record preserves that ruling; it does not introduce a new review policy.

## Decision

**Words:** 「全准」 — Captain, chat, 2026-10-27 (Asia/Taipei).

Verbatim gate resolution reason:

> Captain 「全准」 (chat, 2026-10-27) answering 「需要你決定：第 7 批三張任務的設計（其中兩張已經照第 2 輪訪談修過），要不要一起批准進入實作？我建議全部批准，每一題都照我的建議。」; accepts FO's recommendations

Source: `spacedock-state/dev2:_archive/codex-reader-same-head-unresolved.md`
at state commit `3e25da97432fb22a1a6a7da973730e7c829f3619`,
ideation attempt `gate-attempt:codex-reader-same-head-unresolved-ideation-1`,
resolution `resolution:spacedock:codex-reader-same-head-unresolved:ideation:1`,
recorded at `2026-10-26T17:05:57.33005Z` (2026-10-27 in Asia/Taipei).
The accepted recommendation is D1 under that task's
`## Unresolved decisions for the Captain`; the following rule is a description
of the accepted recommendation, not additional words attributed to the Captain.

**Options considered:**
- A person's resolved mark does not clear a finding on an unchanged head; the
  finding holds until the head moves or the First Officer records its disposition
  in the gate summary (chosen).
- Read GitHub review-thread resolution and let it clear the same-head finding;
  not chosen. The archived design observed no such consumer and this required
  another GraphQL call, pagination and an additional failure path.

**Recommended:** the first option, as D1 recommended and the ideation gate accepted.

**Protects:**
- `kc-dev-flow-2/extensions/codex/codex_review.py` — `state()`, selecting held findings before later no-issues evidence.

A person's resolved mark on a GitHub thread does not clear a Codex finding on an
unchanged head. A later no-issues receipt on that same head does not clear it
either. The reader continues to report the finding and its evidence id.
A new head is read afresh. The First Officer may decline a finding in the gate
summary only under the existing review-disposition rules; that disposition does
not change the reader's verdict. Material findings still require repair or a
Captain waiver, and reviewer P1 findings still require repair and revalidation
or the Captain's recorded waiver, as ADR 0004 requires. ADR 0010 governs
nonblocking findings from round three. Resolving a thread alone grants no waiver.

## Consequences

A finding someone marks resolved on GitHub can still read as findings on the
same head, so the First Officer must record the permitted decline in the gate
summary or move through the existing repair or Captain-waiver route. The reader
adds no thread-resolution request, and a repeated clean receipt does not create
a new round when the deciding evidence id is unchanged. This record does not
prove a code repair, provider behavior or future agent compliance. Revisit only
through a new Captain ruling if an actual use case needs thread-resolution state
to change the reader's verdict.
# 0014. The first officer checks its README against the trunk before dispatch

Date: 2026-10-13

## Status

Accepted

## Context

On 2026-10-13 the first officer (FO) drove four dispatches of one task from a workflow checkout detached at a 2026-10-08 commit. Its `docs/dev2/README.md` was 397 lines behind the 0.21.0 sync on origin/main, so two rules only the newer README carries were missed: dispatch records under `<task>/dispatch/`, and the `package_version.py` hold. `package_version.py` compares the loaded package with the README it is handed, so a stale README passes; nothing compared the README with the trunk's. Spacedock 0.27.0 has no such check (`spacedock --help` lists none, and `status` and `dispatch build` report no README/trunk comparison), and the only mechanical point on its side, `dispatch build`, is outside this package.

## Decision

**Words:** 「准」 — Captain, 2026-10-13, to the combined ideation gate question for this task and two others ("三個都批准，接受下列建議，照 1 → 2 → 3 實作"), which stated the accepted recommendations for this task: D1 fetch and hold if unreachable, D2 strict equality, D3 show the remedy only.

`scripts/workflow_checkout.py <README>` fetches `origin/<trunk>` (trunk from the README's frontmatter) and compares the README's bytes on disk with the trunk's blob at the same path. Exit 0 equal, 1 different, 2 cannot compare. FO runs it before each worker dispatch and on resume, and is told so in `kc-dev-flow-2:dev` (package-owned, so a stale-README FO still reads it) as well as in `references/sd/workflow.md`.

- D1 fetch inside the check; an unreachable origin holds (exit 2). Without a fetch a stale checkout's own `origin/<trunk>` passes it.
- D2 strict equality: a README ahead of the trunk (an unmerged edit) also holds, because "ahead" versus "behind" for one file needs a commit walk this check does not otherwise need.
- D3 FO shows the printed remedy and waits for the Captain; it neither runs the remedy nor moves the checkout, which concurrent sessions may be driving.

**Options considered:**
- the three decisions above as recommended (chosen)
- a second mode of `package_version.py` — rejected: it is a pure file read whose exit 1 means "load a newer package"; a git-backed second meaning on the same code makes the hold ambiguous
- comparing committed blobs (`HEAD:path`) — rejected: FO follows the bytes on disk, and uncommitted edits would pass
- a check inside Spacedock `dispatch build` — outside this package; not available in 0.27.0

**Recommended:** the first option listed in each decision above (fetch and hold; strict equality; show and wait), as the Captain accepted.

## Consequences

The check is prose-enforced: nothing in kc-dev-flow-2 forces FO to run it, and the 2026-10-13 FO's loading of `kc-dev-flow-2:dev` is not recorded, so this ADR does not claim it would have been caught. Only the README is compared, not `_mods/`; a README match is a proxy, since a sync PR changes both together. An offline FO cannot dispatch until the Captain accepts the hold, an FO session started on a branch that edits the README must hold, and each stale checkout costs one Captain turn. A first adoption whose README is not yet on `origin/<trunk>` exits 2 until it merges. Reopen if Spacedock gains a pre-dispatch hook, which would let the check be enforced instead of read.
# 0020. A rise in the workflow word budget needs a Captain ruling recorded with it

Date: 2026-10-17

## Status

Accepted

## Context

`kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py` refused the workflow README only above its budget, so a cut left slack for the next addition. Measured 2026-10-17: 24 commits changed the budget between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-15 (21 raises, 2 cuts; 4420 to 5511 words), and the README stood at 5495 words against 5511. The README is read whole at startup and resume.

## Decision

**Words:** 「文件不應該一直變長，除非可以證明文件內容不是一次性載入，這裡的意義是文件如果一次載入太長，那 llm 的注意力八成會失焦」 — Captain, 2026-10-17, chat; he approved the recommendations of this task's ideation gate with 「那就照建議」 (2026-10-17, gate)

**Options considered:**
- the budget is a start value plus recorded steps and the README count must equal it; a raise step carries the Captain's quoted words and the one moment FO reads the added text, checked for presence only (chosen)
- keep the at-most comparison and ask reviewers to lower the number after a cut — not chosen: it banked 79 words of slack within one review
- a budget per section — not chosen: no measured section limit was proposed

**Recommended:** the first option, as the Captain accepted.

`lint-skills.py` refuses a README whose word count differs from `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_START` plus the `delta` of every entry of `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_STEPS`, in either direction, and names the step to add. A step with a positive `delta` needs a `captain` value holding a 「…」 quote and a `loaded` value naming the moment FO reads the added text; every step needs a `why`.

## Consequences

A cut lowers the budget in the same change, and a raise cannot merge without a quoted ruling. The script checks form and arithmetic: it cannot tell that a quote is the Captain's or that `loaded` is true, and an author who edits `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_START` evades it, so validation compares each quote with the gate record. # 0027. FO-write rules are checked by the script FO already runs at the write

Date: 2026-10-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

The batch-3 observers found four FO-write rules broken days after the write: a Captain ruling recorded before the question it settles (delivery-gate-settles-skipped-checks), a two-part finding declined with one part's reason (chat-only-evidence-observer-blind, special-role-calls-fire-when-needed), a Captain scope change after the backlog gate kept outside `## Captain amendments` (special-role-calls-fire-when-needed), and Release PR #672 merged on the approval of #682 (3m50s later, no task, no `delivery_gate.py` run). Spacedock 0.27.2 runs nothing when FO writes a task file, so each check sits at a script FO is already told to run (ADR 0014: prose-enforced until Spacedock gains a pre-write hook).

Measured as a replay over the committed state of four repositories (this workflow, subspace-relay, subspace-web, qnow; pins in the task's `## Design`): the 0.26.0 decline check held 3 of the 3 declined texts written after it merged although each carried reasons, because it read `( )` only and `e.g.` ended an item; the Scope check held 15 edits made after the backlog gate across the four repositories, all while the ideation gate was open, 9 of them recording a Captain ruling or his words and 6 not; the findings join held the one observed rule-2 violation that has F-numbered findings and none of the three other reports with F bullets. On this machine, read 2026-10-20 from `~/.claude/settings.json`, `permissions.defaultMode` is `auto` and no `allow`, `ask` or `deny` rule names `gh pr merge`, so no permission rule stops a merge deterministically.

## Decision

**Words:** 「要」 (D1), 「Ａ」 (D2, amendment 1 of the task), 「第九題要」 (D3), 「那就不做」 (D4, amendment 2), 「好」 (D5), 「可以」 (D6), 「好」 (D7, amendment 3) — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat, the batch-4 ideation sitting on fo-write-rules-checked.

**Options considered:**
- Rule 3 (D1): a Captain change to Scope between gates is an amendment, checked by `design_surfaces.py check` while `status: ideation`; the README says "between gates" (chosen); leave the 15 events unrecorded
- Rule 4 (D2): the `ASK` line gains "Every other PR, the Release PR included, is asked one at a time." and nothing reads the approved question (chosen); keep the cycle-2 `Merges:` line with head binding, a Captain-only read and a digest check — parked for the guard task
- Rule 4 (D3): the class line reads `class: <class> (verdict ask)` when the saved verdict is `ask`, so the carried-merge line printed on a verdict `ask` is visible (chosen); print the line only for verdict `merge`
- Rule 1 (D4): no check; the observer keeps reading it (chosen, replacing the four-verb phrase check); a phrase check on the follow-ups task
- Rule 2 (D5): read `[ ]` as well as `( )`, end no item at `e.g.` or `i.e.`, hold when declined items are fewer than the newest validation report's `- F<N> Deferred risk:` and `- F<N> Polish:` bullets, and ask validators for one bullet per finding and per part (chosen); parse fix only
- Rule 4 residual (D6): a merge of a PR with no task is outside every check, and this record states why (chosen); claim a stop that was not verified
- Guard (D7): file a task for a `PreToolUse` guard on `gh pr merge` that returns `ask`, covering Claude and Codex (Codex CLI 0.162.1 lists `hooks` as stable with `pre_tool_use`), whose first step is a POC proving the hook stops a merge on each host (chosen); design nothing here

**Recommended:** D1 yes, D2 narrow, D3 yes, D4 the phrase check, D5 all three parts, D6 yes, D7 yes. The Captain overrode D4: he chose no check, on FO's revised recommendation, because there is one case and matching words cannot stop that class of error.

The rule later work must follow: a first officer's write that an observer would otherwise find days later is checked by the script FO already runs at that write where a structured record exists. A Scope change after the backlog gate, found at the ideation gate, is restored or recorded as an amendment with his words and where he said them; a decline is counted against the validator's F-numbered findings; the `ASK` line tells FO that every other PR is asked one at a time. This record amends ADR 0005 (an amendment covers a change made between gates, not only during implementation or at a validation gate) and ADR 0025 (a reason may be in `[ ]`; the join). It records that ADR 0023's reopen condition, a merge landing on an approval whose question did not name it, fired on 2026-10-20 with #672, and ADR 0023's mechanism is unchanged.

## Consequences

Bounded claims, each with what it rests on:
- Rule 4 here is a sentence FO reads. No script checks that an approved question named the merge, so a merge FO makes without running `delivery_gate.py check`, and any merge of a PR with no task (the Release PR, a learning PR), has no check. The premise is the settings read above; it holds for that machine on that date.
- Rule 1 is unchecked. Order cannot discriminate (24 of 24 follow-ups tasks that cite a task PR were filed before the approval they cite) and one case was observed. Reopen it as a read of a structured Captain-rulings field if one lands.
- The Scope check reads git history and the working copy, not what the Captain said in chat. An amendment covers every earlier unrecorded Scope edit, and the check cannot tell whether the amendment is about that edit or whether the words in it are his. It does not run outside `status: ideation`, so a Scope edit after the ideation gate is unchecked (none observed).
- The decline join sees only reports that state findings as F-numbered bullets; a half-reason inside one finding passes, and a stated reason is checked for presence, not truth (ADR 0025).
- Every merge run reads 13 more words, and the class line may carry `(verdict ask)`; a hold of the Scope check prints once, to FO.

Reopen if an observer finds one of rules 2 or 3 broken again with the check present and run, if Spacedock gains a pre-write hook, or when the guard task of D7 reports (if a hook's `ask` does not prompt under auto mode, its route is `deny`, a new question for the Captain).
# Learning

This file collects project-specific practices learned from completed kc-dev-flow-2
tasks. Entries are added or removed as a whole; an entry is never edited in place.
Each entry names an Applicability (when it applies), a Practice (what to do), and
the Evidence behind it.

## Name only an instrument that actually produces the claimed output

### Applicability

When an acceptance criterion, stage report or PR claim in this repository names an
existing script or the pinned release-please fixture as the instrument that
verifies which package(s) a commit is attributed to.

### Practice

Bind the claim only to output that instrument actually produces. Nothing in this
repository routes a commit to a package: scripts/version-parity-check.sh runs only
scripts/release-please-config-check.sh plus python3 version-string comparisons, and
the single release-please import (scripts/release-metadata.test.sh,
probe_release_please_first_tag) builds a first-release tag string through
buildNewVersion/TagName. A commit's resolved package list can only be obtained by
constructing CommitSplit/CommitExclude ad hoc against
scripts/fixtures/release-please-runtime, so a criterion that asserts an existing
repository check does it cannot be satisfied without adding a script.

### Evidence

Verified on origin/main 2026-09-17: `git grep -n "CommitSplit\|CommitExclude"
origin/main -- scripts .github` returns nothing, and the only
`require('release-please')` is scripts/release-metadata.test.sh inside
probe_release_please_first_tag. The cost of not checking is recorded in
spacedock-state/dev2:_archive/release-please-exclude-paths.md at commit 46186575
(validation-gate attempt-1 withdrawal, then the Captain's route-A amendment of
AC-2).

## exclude-paths guards by the key's presence, not its listed paths

### Applicability

When a new top-level workflow-state directory (docs/dev, docs/dev2, docs/ship and
siblings) is introduced, or when extending the contents of a package's
exclude-paths in release-please-config.json is proposed, at the release-please
17.3.0 pinned by scripts/fixtures/release-please-runtime.

### Practice

Do not add the path. The guard is the presence of the exclude-paths key on a
package entry, not its contents: a commit whose changed paths match no package
directory prefix is never bucketed to any package, so that package's
exclude-paths is never consulted for it. Give a package entry that lacks the key a
value matching its siblings instead. Bounded: this holds only for paths outside
every package directory and only for this pinned version; a path inside a package
directory is still compared.

### Evidence

Merge d701df3de01ec3eb0b1e7f5c227d36cdd9d512e1 (iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins#467) adds
one line, kc-dev-flow's "exclude-paths": ["docs/dev"], and adds docs/dev2
nowhere. The measurement behind that narrowing - ["docs/dev"], ["docs/dev2"],
["unrelated-string"] and [] producing an identical drop, with a pre-change
control resolving the empty commit to [kc-dev-flow] - is in
spacedock-state/dev2:_archive/release-please-exclude-paths.md at commit 46186575,
under the AC-2 items of '## Stage Report: implementation' and '## Stage Report:
validation'.

## Hit-test canvas controls; don't trust a keypress to prove clickability

### Applicability

kc-journey-map canvas work that renders an interactive control anywhere inside
tldraw's InFrontOfTheCanvas slot, and any claim that a canvas control is verified
by a browser run.

### Practice

Mount click-target UI with createPortal to document.body as a sibling of
`<Tldraw>` rather than in the in-front slot: .tl-canvas__in-front sets
pointer-events: none by design for canvas-space overlays. In the archived record
(closure revision c560e7ce7109c5ccc4ace87d69ff5506a46e799b), a live
getComputedStyle measurement up the Close button's ancestor chain — button, popup
chrome, dialog, .tl-canvas__in-front — read none at every step even though the
dialog used showModal(); no case was observed where showModal()'s top-layer
promotion overrode that inherited value. For each interactive control, assert
document.elementFromPoint at the control's own bounding-box centre resolves to
that control and dispatch a real pointer click asserting the resulting effect. A
passing Escape or other keypress path does not by itself establish that a control
is clickable: in that same record, the passing runs had exercised only Escape,
which in that run was delivered to the focused element and did not go through
hit-testing, so the Close button's click-through defect went undetected until a
real pointer click was tried.

### Evidence

The Captain clicked Close on the ideation preview and the popup would not close,
while that stage's report had already declared the controls verified by real
Playwright runs; reproduction showed a visible button with a sane bounding box
whose own-centre document.elementFromPoint returned `<html>`, traced to tldraw's
`.tl-canvas__in-front { pointer-events: none }`. The passing runs had exercised
only Escape. kc-journey-map/scripts/popup-browser-check.mjs, landed in merge
ba444ed9b2afc1b6b353286322c9ea5828fed0d6 (iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins#468), now
hit-tests and real-clicks every control across 31 checks, including Close in each
of its three unavailable-state cases (bad ref, bad path, unmapped repo); its
hitTestable helper is the greppable form of the assertion. The defect report and
the measured root cause are in
spacedock-state/dev2:_archive/canvas-document-popup.md at commit
c560e7ce7109c5ccc4ace87d69ff5506a46e799b, under '## Material finding — the Close
control does not work' and '## Correction to FO's own root-cause claim'.

## Map a non-localhost origin at Chromium's DNS layer, not with a Host header

### Applicability

A kc-journey-map browser check that must run against a non-localhost origin, such
as exercising JOURNEY_ALLOWED_HOSTS or a shared-board origin, in an environment
with no root and no writable /etc/hosts.

### Practice

Map the hostname at Chromium's own DNS layer by passing
`--host-resolver-rules=MAP <host> 127.0.0.1` through `agent-browser --args`, then
perform a genuine top-level navigation over that origin. Do not record "needs a
DNS or hosts-file mapping this environment cannot make without root" as a limit
before trying it. In the archived record (closure revision
c560e7ce7109c5ccc4ace87d69ff5506a46e799b), the one attempt to substitute
`agent-browser --headers` with a Host override
(`--headers '{"Host":"sharedorigin.test"}'`) against the real Vite dev server
hung and never completed, which the archived record attributes to Host being a
reserved header CDP would not rewrite for that request; that single observation
is the basis for preferring `--host-resolver-rules` over a `--headers` Host
override.

### Evidence

unachievable in this environment and substituted a curl --resolve HTTP-layer
check; validation disproved that limit with agent-browser

against a bare HTTP server echoing the received Host header and then by running

## Never write git config from a worktree of this repository

### Applicability

failure path by writing git configuration (for example `git remote set-url origin
...`, `git config`) from inside a worktree checkout, including the Captain's main
checkout or any worktree of the repository.

### Practice

Do not write git config in any worktree of this repository: every worktree shares
one config, so one write changes every checkout. Run such a step only in a throwaway
`git clone` in a temp directory, and say so in the dispatch scope notes and in the
acceptance script. If a shared value is changed by mistake, restore it from a
recorded original, so record the original value before any config read-modify step.
Bounded: one observed incident; this does not show the ban alone prevented a repeat,
since the acceptance script was also moved into a throwaway clone.

## List every input before promising a verdict survives later history

### Applicability

A kc-dev-flow-2 task in this repository that designs or reviews a check run over
committed history (such as the state-branch laws runner) and promises that a
violation, once committed, keeps its verdict after later commits (for example "stays
red until an anchor moves"), or that answers a review finding of the form "a later
change erases a committed violation".

### Practice

Before the design gate, list every input the verdict reads (files read at the run
revision, task files enumerated at the tip, the README or config passed in at run
time) and write the persistence promise as one property test: after the event,
commit every later change the history allows (edit, delete, archive, rename, and a
change to each run-time input) and require the same exit code and output. When a
review finding of this class arrives, treat it as a finding about that list: add the
input it names and every sibling input to the list and to the test in the same
cycle, instead of repairing the one reported read. If an input cannot be pinned to
the event, narrow or drop the promise in the design and ask the Captain, rather than
shipping an absolute that later history can undo. Uncertain: whether this ordering
would have avoided the rework, since the Captain's actual ruling was to drop the
promise.

## Measure the words FO reads at each moment, not one file's size

### Applicability

A kc-dev-flow-2 change whose goal is to cut what First Officer (FO) reads, such as
moving rule text out of the adopted README (references/sd/workflow.md) into a mod,
a script's printed output or another file, where acceptance is stated as a word
count.

### Practice

State the acceptance number as the words FO reads at each lifecycle moment
(startup, idle on an open PR, idle on a merged PR, after the archive, the merge
ask): every passage and every script output that instructs a step due at that
moment, counted the same way for the unchanged base and for the candidate, with
each moment required to fall below its base. Do not accept the size of the one
file the text left (for example WORKFLOW_WORD_BUDGET in
kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py) as the measure, because that number can fall
while FO's total reading rises. Bounded: one task; the redesign also gave each
step one home, so the count is not shown to be the only cause of the reduction;
the recount script lives only in the archived task's validation folder, not in the
repository; and a validator found the first recount script under-counted one
moment, so recount with an independent copy.

## Compare a shrunk rule with what its script rejects before cutting it

### Applicability

A kc-dev-flow-2 change in this repository that shortens a README
(references/sd/workflow.md) rule into a pointer to a script that checks it, such as
dispatch_records.py, design_surfaces.py or observer_check.py, to meet the workflow
word budget.

### Practice

Before cutting a clause, compare each clause of the sentence with what the script
rejects, not only with what its failure messages say: run the script on one input
that the dropped clause forbids, and keep the clause in the README whenever the
script lets that input through. For each kept clause, pin the README phrase with a
need string in test_sd_dispatch.py, because pins written for the removed parts do
not cover it. Bounded: one task; the sentence was restored after an external review
round, so the record does not show that this comparison would have found the gap
before review, and validation had passed the first candidate with the clause
missing.

## Update every parser of a script mode in the change that adds a new output line

### Applicability

A kc-dev-flow-2 change in this repository that makes a script mode print a new kind
of line, such as a new diagnostic from `dispatch_records.py --names`, when another

# 0020. A rise in the workflow word budget needs a Captain ruling recorded with it

Date: 2026-10-17

## Status

Accepted

## Context

`kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py` refused the workflow README only above its budget, so a cut left slack for the next addition. Measured 2026-10-17: 24 commits changed the budget between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-15 (21 raises, 2 cuts; 4420 to 5511 words), and the README stood at 5495 words against 5511. The README is read whole at startup and resume.

## Decision

**Words:** 「文件不應該一直變長，除非可以證明文件內容不是一次性載入，這裡的意義是文件如果一次載入太長，那 llm 的注意力八成會失焦」 — Captain, 2026-10-17, chat; he approved the recommendations of this task's ideation gate with 「那就照建議」 (2026-10-17, gate)

**Options considered:**
- the budget is a start value plus recorded steps and the README count must equal it; a raise step carries the Captain's quoted words and the one moment FO reads the added text, checked for presence only (chosen)
- keep the at-most comparison and ask reviewers to lower the number after a cut — not chosen: it banked 79 words of slack within one review
- a budget per section — not chosen: no measured section limit was proposed

**Recommended:** the first option, as the Captain accepted.

`lint-skills.py` refuses a README whose word count differs from `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_START` plus the `delta` of every entry of `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_STEPS`, in either direction, and names the step to add. A step with a positive `delta` needs a `captain` value holding a 「…」 quote and a `loaded` value naming the moment FO reads the added text; every step needs a `why`.

## Consequences

A cut lowers the budget in the same change, and a raise cannot merge without a quoted ruling. The script checks form and arithmetic: it cannot tell that a quote is the Captain's or that `loaded` is true, and an author who edits `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_START` evades it, so validation compares each quote with the gate record. Two pull requests that both edit the README conflict on the steps and the later one recounts. Reopen if a raise lands whose quote is not the Captain's.
# 0027. FO-write rules are checked by the script FO already runs at the write

Date: 2026-10-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

The batch-3 observers found four FO-write rules broken days after the write: a Captain ruling recorded before the question it settles (delivery-gate-settles-skipped-checks), a two-part finding declined with one part's reason (chat-only-evidence-observer-blind, special-role-calls-fire-when-needed), a Captain scope change after the backlog gate kept outside `## Captain amendments` (special-role-calls-fire-when-needed), and Release PR #672 merged on the approval of #682 (3m50s later, no task, no `delivery_gate.py` run). Spacedock 0.27.2 runs nothing when FO writes a task file, so each check sits at a script FO is already told to run (ADR 0014: prose-enforced until Spacedock gains a pre-write hook).

Measured as a replay over the committed state of four repositories (this workflow, subspace-relay, subspace-web, qnow; pins in the task's `## Design`): the 0.26.0 decline check held 3 of the 3 declined texts written after it merged although each carried reasons, because it read `( )` only and `e.g.` ended an item; the Scope check held 15 edits made after the backlog gate across the four repositories, all while the ideation gate was open, 9 of them recording a Captain ruling or his words and 6 not; the findings join held the one observed rule-2 violation that has F-numbered findings and none of the three other reports with F bullets. On this machine, read 2026-10-20 from `~/.claude/settings.json`, `permissions.defaultMode` is `auto` and no `allow`, `ask` or `deny` rule names `gh pr merge`, so no permission rule stops a merge deterministically.

## Decision

**Words:** 「要」 (D1), 「Ａ」 (D2, amendment 1 of the task), 「第九題要」 (D3), 「那就不做」 (D4, amendment 2), 「好」 (D5), 「可以」 (D6), 「好」 (D7, amendment 3) — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat, the batch-4 ideation sitting on fo-write-rules-checked.

**Options considered:**
- Rule 3 (D1): a Captain change to Scope between gates is an amendment, checked by `design_surfaces.py check` while `status: ideation`; the README says "between gates" (chosen); leave the 15 events unrecorded
- Rule 4 (D2): the `ASK` line gains "Every other PR, the Release PR included, is asked one at a time." and nothing reads the approved question (chosen); keep the cycle-2 `Merges:` line with head binding, a Captain-only read and a digest check — parked for the guard task
- Rule 4 (D3): the class line reads `class: <class> (verdict ask)` when the saved verdict is `ask`, so the carried-merge line printed on a verdict `ask` is visible (chosen); print the line only for verdict `merge`
- Rule 1 (D4): no check; the observer keeps reading it (chosen, replacing the four-verb phrase check); a phrase check on the follow-ups task
- Rule 2 (D5): read `[ ]` as well as `( )`, end no item at `e.g.` or `i.e.`, hold when declined items are fewer than the newest validation report's `- F<N> Deferred risk:` and `- F<N> Polish:` bullets, and ask validators for one bullet per finding and per part (chosen); parse fix only
- Rule 4 residual (D6): a merge of a PR with no task is outside every check, and this record states why (chosen); claim a stop that was not verified
- Guard (D7): file a task for a `PreToolUse` guard on `gh pr merge` that returns `ask`, covering Claude and Codex (Codex CLI 0.162.1 lists `hooks` as stable with `pre_tool_use`), whose first step is a POC proving the hook stops a merge on each host (chosen); design nothing here

**Recommended:** D1 yes, D2 narrow, D3 yes, D4 the phrase check, D5 all three parts, D6 yes, D7 yes. The Captain overrode D4: he chose no check, on FO's revised recommendation, because there is one case and matching words cannot stop that class of error.

The rule later work must follow: a first officer's write that an observer would otherwise find days later is checked by the script FO already runs at that write where a structured record exists. A Scope change after the backlog gate, found at the ideation gate, is restored or recorded as an amendment with his words and where he said them; a decline is counted against the validator's F-numbered findings; the `ASK` line tells FO that every other PR is asked one at a time. This record amends ADR 0005 (an amendment covers a change made between gates, not only during implementation or at a validation gate) and ADR 0025 (a reason may be in `[ ]`; the join). It records that ADR 0023's reopen condition, a merge landing on an approval whose question did not name it, fired on 2026-10-20 with #672, and ADR 0023's mechanism is unchanged.

## Consequences

Bounded claims, each with what it rests on:
- Rule 4 here is a sentence FO reads. No script checks that an approved question named the merge, so a merge FO makes without running `delivery_gate.py check`, and any merge of a PR with no task (the Release PR, a learning PR), has no check. The premise is the settings read above; it holds for that machine on that date.
- Rule 1 is unchecked. Order cannot discriminate (24 of 24 follow-ups tasks that cite a task PR were filed before the approval they cite) and one case was observed. Reopen it as a read of a structured Captain-rulings field if one lands.
- The Scope check reads git history and the working copy, not what the Captain said in chat. An amendment covers every earlier unrecorded Scope edit, and the check cannot tell whether the amendment is about that edit or whether the words in it are his. It does not run outside `status: ideation`, so a Scope edit after the ideation gate is unchecked (none observed).
- The decline join sees only reports that state findings as F-numbered bullets; a half-reason inside one finding passes, and a stated reason is checked for presence, not truth (ADR 0025).
- Every merge run reads 13 more words, and the class line may carry `(verdict ask)`; a hold of the Scope check prints once, to FO.

Reopen if an observer finds one of rules 2 or 3 broken again with the check present and run, if Spacedock gains a pre-write hook, or when the guard task of D7 reports (if a hook's `ask` does not prompt under auto mode, its route is `deny`, a new question for the Captain).

Read 2026-11-07 at the pins named here.

- **Spacedock** (`spacedock-dev/spacedock` origin/main 324c61588, and tag v0.27.2, the installed and CI-pinned binary): `dispatch build --stamp` (`runStamp` in `internal/dispatch/stamp.go`) stamps `started`/`worktree`, makes one path-scoped state commit `dispatch: <slug> entering <stage>`, publishes it and creates the worktree; `runBuildFields` in `build.go` then writes only `/tmp/spacedock-dispatch/<name>.md`. Nothing writes `<task>/dispatch/`. Mods have four hook points only (`git grep -hoE '## Hook: [a-z-]+'`: startup, merge, idle, shutdown); none runs at dispatch. The build also cannot know the record's `Model:` line: on Claude its envelope `model` is the Agent enum (`opus`), and a Paseo dispatch's model and `Roster:` come from `model_roster.py`, which Spacedock does not read.
- **The seam the design uses:** `entityCommitPaths` puts the task's companion folder `<slug>/` into the stamp commit (`git add -A -- <slug>.md <slug>/`). Probe on 0.27.2 (`/tmp/stamp-probe.3Byi`, split-root fixture with this workflow's README): an uncommitted `probe/dispatch/ideation-1.md` was committed by `dispatch: probe entering ideation`; on a second build for the same stage, with `started` already set, `ideation-2.md` alone was committed by the same subject. `spacedock state commit probe` committed an uncommitted `implementation-1.md` as `state: update probe`, which covers `--advance`, where `--stamp` is refused.
- **kc-dev-flow-2** (origin/main 139feeaee, 0.35.0): `dispatch_records.py` checks a record and writes none; `replay_dispatch.py` wraps `dispatch build` for replays and copies the dispatch file into its run folder, not a record. `git grep 'dispatch build'` finds no other writer.
- **Adopters** (subspace-relay, subspace-web, qnow, `origin/HEAD`, read-only `git grep -lE 'dispatch build|dispatch_records|/dispatch/[a-z]+-'`): their synced `docs/dev2*/README.md`, plus qnow history notes; no wrapper and no record writer.

So Spacedock cannot write the record without an upstream change in a repository the Captain does not own, and it would still lack the model line. The package wraps the build instead.

### PRFAQ

**kc-dev-flow-2 records every worker dispatch as it builds it.** FO now builds a worker dispatch with one package script. The script writes `<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` from the same checklist and scope-notes files it hands to `spacedock dispatch build --stamp`, adds the model and the workflow checkout's SHA, runs both `dispatch_records.py` checks, and only then builds. The stamp's own state commit carries the record, so a record cannot be missing, written after the fact, or different from what the worker received.

- *What does FO still write?* The checklist and the scope notes, as today, and the model, roster, candidate and symptom values as flags. The script writes the header, the sections and the cycle number.
- *What if a part is missing?* The script removes the file it wrote, prints the checker's lines, and builds nothing. Its message starts `dispatch_stage: dispatch not built;`, so FO does not mistake it for a `dispatch build` failure that allows break-glass dispatch.
- *What if the build fails?* Spacedock's stderr and exit code pass through unchanged. If the record was not committed, the script removes it; an identical immediate rerun reuses the committed number instead of minting a new one.
- *Follow-up messages to a live worker?* Not covered: FO still saves those by hand.
- *Acceptance evidence:* a test against the CI-pinned Spacedock 0.27.2 binary (AC-1 to AC-6), and the README and pinned tests (AC-7).

### Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  G[FO: task status equals the stage] --> W["dispatch_stage.py: build flags, --model, optional --roster / --candidate / --symptom"]
  W --> U{flag values valid?}
  U -- no --> U2[usage error, exit 2, no file written]
  U -- yes --> N{"newest record of this stage identical and added by the state HEAD commit?"}
  N -- yes --> K[reuse its number, write nothing]
  N -- no --> R["write task/dispatch/stage-N.md, N = newest + 1"]
  K --> C
  R --> C{"dispatch_records.py folder check and --names --strict"}
  C -- nonzero --> X["remove the file it wrote, print the checker lines, exit 1, no build"]
  C -- zero --> A{--advance?}
  A -- no --> S[spacedock dispatch build --stamp]
  A -- yes --> V[spacedock dispatch build --advance]
  S -- nonzero --> F["remove the record if uncommitted; pass Spacedock stderr and exit code"]
  V -- nonzero --> F
  S -- zero --> E["stamp commit carries the record; envelope JSON on stdout"]
  V -- zero --> SC{spacedock state commit slug}
  SC -- nonzero --> F2["exit 1, envelope withheld, record left for an identical rerun"]
  SC -- zero --> E
  E --> P["FO spawns the worker from the envelope (Agent or Paseo create_agent)"]
```
